safety.shared_testnet: Only our operator APIs, loopback providers, netuid 521 identities/stake, and capped read RPC may be exercised. No chain-wide denial-of-service, third-party proxy, or third-party identity action is authorized.
safety.local_runtime: Chain-wide exploit reproduction runs only against the release-locked M0A runtime clone. The live campaign runs a bounded emulator or detection sentinel for those rows.
safety.lifecycle: Every actor starts before the release happy path, remains active through final reconciliation, and must stop cleanly after all happy-path assertions settle.

rows.vector: A free-rider copies a prior honest or prior-consensus vector instead of measuring current miner utility.
rows.preconditions: The attacker can observe an older revealed vector and has validator stake.
rows.oracle: A minority stale vector cannot move the stake-weighted median away from the current honest vector; stale-vector divergence and validator trust are recorded.

rows.vector: A last mover observes revealed weights and follows the emerging consensus to earn dividends without independent work.
rows.preconditions: Commit/reveal ordering, reveal visibility, or reveal windows permit a follower to react.
rows.oracle: Commit/reveal remains enabled and the follower model cannot alter minority consensus; commit/reveal runtime state and finalized ordering remain stable.

rows.vector: A coordinated minority inflates its own miners or pools while concealing affiliation.
rows.preconditions: Coordinated validator stake remains below kappa but assigns extreme self-weight.
rows.oracle: The cabal-only UID is clipped to zero below kappa and affiliation masks still cover every controlled pool/fleet UID.

rows.vector: A cabal zeros honest rivals while boosting its own cohort.
rows.preconditions: Minority validators coordinate low weights on honest servers.
rows.oracle: Below-kappa knifing does not reduce honest consensus weights or produce a cabal incentive gain.

rows.vector: Stake or permit churn moves an adversarial coalition across the kappa or validator-permit boundary.
rows.preconditions: Stake concentration or validator dropout changes active stake between epochs.
rows.oracle: Sweeps explicitly identify the protection boundary; the live campaign halts if honest active stake or required validator permits fall below policy.

rows.vector: A delayed validator copies an early evaluator after consensus becomes visible, while stake or validator-permit churn attempts to preserve or reacquire historical bond advantage.
rows.preconditions: The attacker can observe prior weights or consensus and can enter, leave, or cross the validator-permit boundary between epochs.
rows.oracle: Across current/previous-consensus and sigmoid-steepness sweeps, the early independent evaluator retains more than its 60% stake share, the delayed copier receives less than its 40% stake share, and permit loss clears rather than preserves the accumulated bond.

rows.vector: A validator withholds, reveals late, reveals invalid data, replays an expired commit, or accumulates pending commits.
rows.preconditions: The attacker controls its own registered hotkey and submits malformed lifecycle transitions.
rows.oracle: The exact runtime rejects invalid/expired transitions without mutating the last finalized intent; live sentinels detect missing honest reveals and pending-intent growth.

rows.vector: Consecutive fee-free set/commit/reveal transactions pass pool validation but fail the in-dispatch rate limit while consuming the normal block class.
rows.preconditions: An affected runtime and one qualifying registered hotkey; affected versions place the rate limit only in dispatch.
rows.oracle: The release-locked runtime rejects over-rate transactions before inclusion; shared-testnet execution is forbidden and the live sentinel records inclusion latency only.

rows.vector: One validator disappears, restarts, disagrees with another validator, or returns with stale intent state while hostile traffic continues.
rows.preconditions: At least two independent validators and block-scheduled restart faults.
rows.oracle: The surviving validator remains live, restarted intent recovery is exact, and reconciliation contains no ambiguous or duplicate submission.

rows.vector: A miner or fleet churns registrations, gets pruned, re-registers, or attempts to inherit stale reputation and bindings under a new UID.
rows.preconditions: Registration capacity, burn movement, or pruning makes a UID reusable.
rows.oracle: Every score/binding is keyed by hotkey, generation, effective epoch and live UID; stale generations never receive weight or payout.

rows.vector: A registered hotkey publishes a valid but unexpected commitment Data variant or a multi-field value that crashes a shape-assuming metagraph client or is misread by a suffix-only authorization parser.
rows.preconditions: Arbitrary registered hotkeys can publish any runtime-valid CommitmentInfo field sequence and a fleet observer consumes native commitment storage.
rows.oracle: The release decodes the full pinned runtime-447 Registration encoding, accepts exactly one nonzero Sha256 field, and returns an attributed error for ResetBondsFlag, alternate variants, extra fields, truncation, or trailing bytes without panicking.

rows.vector: Hotkey swaps or replacements reset measurement state, evade cooldowns, or retain stale commitments/bindings.
rows.preconditions: The identity owner performs a subnet-scoped or all-subnets hotkey swap.
rows.oracle: Patched runtime state migrates or resets exactly as specified; UR bindings require a new generation and effective epoch before use.

rows.vector: A restricted proxy reaches a newly added or duplicate alias call and escalates into coldkey, hotkey, or subnet-owner control.
rows.preconditions: A victim granted a scoped proxy and the runtime proxy filter omitted a live call or alias.
rows.oracle: The exact runtime denies every equivalent privileged call for restricted proxy types; no third-party proxy is touched on shared testnet.

rows.vector: Fresh root-staking coldkeys or coldkey swaps leave dead entries in the dense auto-claim index, diluting useful per-block claims and growing state without bound.
rows.preconditions: An attacker can fund many distinct coldkeys or repeatedly coldkey-swap a root-staked position.
rows.oracle: The v447 inverse operation removes fully unstaked keys, swap-removes the last entry into each hole, and preserves the forward/reverse dense-index bijection; shared-testnet sentinels observe runtime identity and finalized-block latency without creating global state.

rows.vector: A root hotkey swap targets a seemingly clean key with a residual claimed watermark; merging old plus residual claimed state suppresses future dividends.
rows.preconditions: The actor controls both keys and the destination has no root stake/claimable rate but retains a nonzero legacy claimed watermark.
rows.oracle: The v447 root-cleanliness gate rejects every nonempty basket, stake, claimable, or claimed destination before mutation; a clean move preserves the claimed watermark and exact future owed amount.

rows.vector: A root staker exits or reduces a position but accrued beta-basket rewards remain silently claimable only through a second call, leaving operator or custodian assets invisible and dependent on residual lookup state.
rows.preconditions: A release-controlled coldkey has root stake with an accrued validator basket and reduces or exits that position.
rows.oracle: Every partial/full exit inventory records principal plus the proportional accrued basket, exact floor remainder, second-call requirement and post-exit claimability; mainnet automation must claim or prove no hidden basket remains.

rows.vector: A proxy stake is submitted without the default MEV shield, allowing a same-direction transaction to move the alpha reserve before inclusion and force materially worse execution.
rows.preconditions: An online signer uses proxy staking and the client cannot wrap the proxied call with the runtime MEV-shield mechanism.
rows.oracle: The constant-product ordering model quantifies unshielded loss and proves a bound minimum-output call rejects the hostile ordering; release automation refuses unshielded proxy staking.

rows.vector: Code confuses EVM H160 and native SS58 authority, or wei (18 decimals) and rao (9 decimals), causing mis-authorization or value amplification.
rows.preconditions: A workflow bridges EVM and native accounts or converts TAO units.
rows.oracle: Typed domains, exact integer conversions, mirror authorization and budget ceilings reject cross-domain substitution and 10^9-scale errors.

rows.vector: A runtime upgrade changes metadata, storage encoding, API presence, precompile code/selectors, transaction version, or semantics beneath a deployed contract/client.
rows.preconditions: The shared chain upgrades while the campaign is live.
rows.oracle: Pinned spec/transaction/state versions, API capability probes, code hashes and finalized checkpoint agreement remain exact; any drift halts.

rows.vector: Registration burn changes or a competing registration front-runs the UID/burn assumption between plan and inclusion.
rows.preconditions: Burn, capacity, or metagraph changes after the approved plan snapshot.
rows.oracle: Every registration is limit-bounded and postconditioned to the planned hotkey/coldkey; plan or live-state drift invalidates execution.

rows.vector: A new subnet registration at the global subnet limit displaces an out-of-immunity subnet with the lowest moving alpha price; hostile liquidity or emission pressure can reduce the safety margin before launch operators react.
rows.preconditions: The global subnet limit is full, this subnet is outside its network immunity period, and its moving price reaches the pruning boundary.
rows.oracle: At a common finalized block, private and public precompiles agree that netuid 521 still has nonzero UID count and spot price while spot and moving price trajectories are retained in campaign evidence; mainnet launch separately requires a nonzero moving price and reviewed pruning margin.

rows.vector: An attacker depresses TAO/alpha reserves until coinbase swaps fail; negative protocol-flow accounting can then be interpreted as positive emission contribution, and a spend-before-failed-swap path can strand TAO outside subnet accounting.
rows.preconditions: A well-funded attacker can materially drain a dynamic subnet's reserves and force the coinbase excess-TAO swap failure branch.
rows.oracle: TAO and alpha reserves remain nonzero and their full campaign minima are retained; the bounded signed-flow model clamps net outflow to zero contribution rather than rewarding it. Mainnet remains no-go until the pinned runtime fixes the open upstream accounting paths or exact-runtime proof shows them unreachable.

rows.vector: A private/public RPC lags, equivocates, omits historical state, rate-limits, or returns inconsistent finalized EVM/native views.
rows.preconditions: Multiple independent read endpoints and archive queries are available.
rows.oracle: Finalized heads converge within three blocks, common-height hashes agree, archive queries succeed and EVM/native checkpoints match under capped pressure.

rows.vector: The Bittensor SDK anchors an at-most-eight-block MEV-shield mortal era at the finalized head, so best-head finality lag can make an otherwise valid CRv4 commit stale before transaction-pool admission.
rows.preconditions: A validator uses the SDK MEV-shield submission path while best head is eight or more blocks ahead of finalized head.
rows.oracle: The live actor records best-minus-finalized lag and the exact SDK expiry predicate continuously. Release CRv4 writes use a directly signed immortal extrinsic with a durable exact nonce, exact-byte replay, runtime identity gate, and canonical finalized receipt, so this SDK-only mortality failure cannot silently lose a release intent.

rows.vector: Bittensor Dendrite sends miner requests over plaintext HTTP and does not authenticate responses, permitting passive disclosure and active response forgery by an on-path attacker.
rows.preconditions: An attacker can observe or alter a non-loopback miner/operator transport path.
rows.oracle: Non-loopback provider configuration rejects plaintext HTTP/WebSocket endpoints. During the live campaign, tampered copies of real signed ASSIGN/FINAL responses fail canonical Ed25519 verification while the original happy path remains valid; loopback plaintext is allowed only inside the isolated simulator.

rows.vector: The Bittensor Synapse default hashes an empty required-field set, producing a constant body hash that does not bind the request or response payload.
rows.preconditions: A signed protocol message relies on the SDK default empty required_hash_fields value instead of a versioned canonical full-message encoding.
rows.oracle: UR verification signs explicit canonical encodings rather than Synapse.body_hash. Every identity, nonce, depth, path, timing, egress and coverage mutation changes the signed message and is rejected continuously; evidence artifacts independently retain content hashes and signer domains.

rows.vector: Bittensor Axon.default_verify historically guarded verification with a truthiness check, so an omitted signature skipped cryptographic verification and let a caller impersonate a registered high-stake validator.
rows.preconditions: A protocol verifier treats an absent or empty signature as a reason to skip verification rather than as an invalid fixed-width input.
rows.oracle: The live actor continuously alternates absent and wrong fixed-width SEED signatures against each loopback operator. Both fail with HTTP 400 before trail state is created, while signed control trails complete under the claimed validator key.

rows.vector: Bounded concurrent status, stats, proofs, history and malformed requests consume API, PostgreSQL, Redis or object-store resources while epoch work runs.
rows.preconditions: The managed operator APIs and dependencies are live.
rows.oracle: No 5xx, bounded response size/latency/error rate, no restart storm, and happy-path deadlines/reconciliation remain intact.

rows.vector: A caller compares real and poisoned SEED/EXTEND responses, timing, identifiers, proof shape or durable side effects to build a poison oracle.
rows.preconditions: The caller controls valid and unknown source addresses and validator keys.
rows.oracle: Real and poison responses retain valid signed shapes and bounded timing/size deltas; poison never changes provider statistics or durable proof history.

rows.vector: Identical or reordered EXTEND requests race to double-confirm, rewrite a trail, duplicate statistics, or return inconsistent cached proofs.
rows.preconditions: A caller owns a valid validator key and can replay signed bodies through the assigned provider source.
rows.oracle: One mutation wins, contenders receive bounded busy/idempotent responses, final replay is byte-identical and each assigned hop is counted once.

rows.vector: An attacker rotates VPK/client IDs or malformed bodies to evade per-key limits and create unbounded trail state.
rows.preconditions: Unknown callers can reach unauthenticated POST /verify from controlled source IPs.
rows.oracle: The source-IP hard bound triggers regardless of VPK rotation; malformed input never causes 5xx or unbounded durable state.

rows.vector: An operator withholds, truncates, mutates, re-signs inconsistently, or serves different payout artifacts/history for one finalized entitlement.
rows.preconditions: At least one finalized entitlement and public history object exists.
rows.oracle: Content hash, EIP-712 signer, policy/deployment identity and on-chain root all agree across both public origins and MinIO history; tampered copies fail locally.

rows.vector: A miner recognizes validator routes or cadence and serves only probes while abandoning ordinary users.
rows.preconditions: Miner can classify source, timing, route depth, or validator identity.
rows.oracle: Shadow/poison routing remains indistinguishable, randomized continuous probes overlap happy traffic, and service quality changes appear in independent operator-specific scores.

rows.vector: Colluding providers short-circuit or replay trails, forge apparent coverage, or share a route endpoint.
rows.preconditions: Multiple provider client IDs coordinate routing and signatures.
rows.oracle: Server-selected fresh hops, source-IP attribution, canonical signatures, monotone server time and unique path IDs reject repeats/short circuits.

rows.vector: A fleet rents, shares, rotates or reassigns prefixes/client IDs to claim duplicate head coverage or evade head/tail accounting.
rows.preconditions: Multiple clients or fleets can present the same egress prefix over time.
rows.oracle: Keyed prefix claims split exactly across concurrent fleets, generations are effective next epoch, and a client/UID cannot bind to two active identities.

rows.vector: A validator hides common control through alternate coldkeys, operator roles, fleets or deposit identities and weights itself.
rows.preconditions: Economic control spans identities not captured by the declared relationship graph.
rows.oracle: All explicitly controlled pool/fleet/self UIDs are zero-masked and an independent validator still observes/weights every legitimate cohort; residual off-chain beneficial ownership is documented.

rows.vector: A deposit races a conviction tier boundary, replays across epochs/operators, credits the wrong NO, or exceeds epoch/campaign caps.
rows.preconditions: Signed deposits and conviction changes occur near snapshot/finalization boundaries.
rows.oracle: Domain, signer, nonce, NO, policy and epoch snapshot are atomic; caps and exact received funds hold under replay/reorder.

rows.vector: An operator omits a miner, duplicates leaves, underallocates, changes a payout wallet, or publishes a root/artifact that does not conserve captured value.
rows.preconditions: The operator constructs a payout artifact and root from measured provider rows.
rows.oracle: Deterministic largest-remainder allocation, sorted unique leaves, wallet snapshot and on-chain conservation reproduce the exact root independently.

rows.vector: A valid deposit/root/governance signature is replayed on another chain, contract, NO, epoch, policy, nonce or after its deadline.
rows.preconditions: An attacker obtains an old valid EIP-712 signature or reorders signed calls.
rows.oracle: Every changed domain/message component and every replay/expired deadline reverts without partial state.

rows.vector: A precompile/callback reenters, a transfer receives less than requested, or keeper/root/funding calls are front-run and reordered into partial state.
rows.preconditions: External/precompile calls occur during deposit, capture, funding, claim or reserve operations.
rows.oracle: Non-reentrancy, checks-effects-interactions, exact received-funds accounting and state-machine guards preserve conservation under every reorder/failure point.

rows.vector: A malicious coordinator upgrade, owner, guardian or operator role attempts to rewrite finalized entitlements, withdraw principal, or block immutable claims.
rows.preconditions: Testnet single-owner governance or future mainnet 2-of-3 Safe can schedule privileged actions.
rows.oracle: The live hostile testnet implementation cannot mutate immutable vault/reserve custody; pause stops new risk while finalized claims remain callable.

rows.vector: Keepers arrive late, roots are missed, claims straddle TTL/grace, or relayers replay/double-claim while services restart.
rows.preconditions: Block-scheduled operator/keeper/claim-daemon faults cross settlement boundaries.
rows.oracle: Value carries only to the same operator, valid claims settle once, expired claims reject, restart recovery is exact and liabilities remain conserved.

rows.vector: Repeated rounding, user-controlled collection sizes or gas exhaustion create value drift, stuck settlement, or unbounded operator/miner loops.
rows.preconditions: Many leaves/operators or adversarial fractional shares approach size/gas bounds.
rows.oracle: All loops/caps are bounded, largest-remainder totals are exact, deploy/runtime sizes fit limits, and worst-case gas stays below the planned ceiling.

rows.vector: A downstream swap, transfer, burn, recycle or fee step fails after an earlier balance/stake write; the call returns failure but leaves partial state, or marks a claim paid without transferring value.
rows.preconditions: A composite runtime/precompile path performs two or more writes and a later transfer or price-limited swap fails.
rows.oracle: Every forced downstream failure restores the byte-exact pre-state, never advances a paid watermark, and never emits a successful value event; the live reserve sentinel remains conserved.

rows.vector: Hotkey/coldkey migration omits or downgrades root dividends, conviction, child assignments, per-subnet take, or one contributor's lock mass.
rows.preconditions: A live identity with non-default locks, conviction, root entitlement, child graph or take is migrated or force-unlocked.
rows.oracle: Migration is bijective and lossless across every field, perpetual locks remain perpetual, aggregate locked mass equals contributor sums, and the old identity has no residual authority or entitlement.

rows.vector: A zero-share or repeated partial-fill order is charged, closed, over-filled or double-debited when it should reject or replay idempotently.
rows.preconditions: An order has a zero pro-rata allocation, a residual smaller than the requested fill, or the same fill identifier is resubmitted.
rows.oracle: Zero-share and over-fill requests leave byte-exact state; a valid partial fill conserves debit/credit/remaining once and an identical replay is a no-op.

rows.vector: Dust, failed protocol injection, migration omissions, accumulated flow toggles or cap arithmetic silently change total issuance, reserves or emissions.
rows.preconditions: A transfer creates dust, protocol liquidity cannot be injected, a reserve schema migrates, or a disabled flow accumulator is re-enabled.
rows.oracle: Account sums equal total issuance after explicit burn, old and new reserve totals match exactly, failed injections preserve emissions for retry, and stale flow is never injected as one block.

rows.vector: Unbounded root iteration, zero-gas precompile work, failed fee-free calls, archive RPC memory growth or transaction-pool tag corruption exhausts a node or panics a runtime service.
rows.preconditions: An attacker can submit a bounded-but-expensive runtime call family or sustain costly archive/precompile queries.
rows.oracle: Exact-runtime attack regressions remain bounded and non-panicking; the shared-testnet actor performs only capped reads while finalized lag and request p99 remain within policy.

rows.vector: An unprivileged account jumps the stored drand round so future sequential rounds are rejected and timelocked weight or MEV-shield reveals cannot complete.
rows.preconditions: The randomness pallet accepts a candidate round far beyond the bounded next round without proving the intervening chain.
rows.oracle: Only monotonic bounded round advancement mutates state; a far-future round is rejected without moving the watermark, and live commit/reveal progress remains finalized.

rows.vector: Empty child assignments, self-loops or indirect cycles create ambiguous delegation, reward loops or unbounded graph traversal.
rows.preconditions: A hotkey can replace its child set with zero entries or a graph edge that reaches itself.
rows.oracle: Empty, self-loop and indirect-cycle updates reject without state change; an acyclic bounded graph is accepted and traversed within its node cap.

rows.vector: Lease termination removes the only usable proxy/account while owner-cut alpha, locks and identity indexes remain under an unspendable derived coldkey.
rows.preconditions: A finite subnet lease accrues owner-cut alpha and locks before termination transfers ownership.
rows.oracle: Termination atomically repatriates all alpha and lock mass, removes every derived-coldkey index, and preserves total value before proxy removal.

rows.vector: Unequal queued registrations are backed only by the maximum lock, or the initial owner receives an uncontested floor-price allocation and exits into later buyers.
rows.preconditions: Multiple queued registrations coexist, or the subnet owner can receive initial alpha before competitive price discovery.
rows.oracle: The emulator backs the sum of all live locks and rejects preferential unpriced owner allocation; live moving/spot price, reserve and eviction sentinels never cross their stop conditions.

rows.vector: Concentrated or depleted liquidity makes a subnet permanently non-functional, strands price-limited input, or drops protocol emissions that cannot be injected at current Balancer bounds.
rows.preconditions: TAO/alpha reserves approach an extreme ratio or an injection/swap hits its price or Balancer limit.
rows.oracle: Failed price-limited operations are atomic and retryable, emissions remain pending rather than dropped, and live spot/moving prices and both reserves stay positive with reviewed margins.

rows.vector: Simulator-owned PostgreSQL, Redis, the loopback Subtensor RPC proxy, or a process restarts, loses transient state, returns stale data, or induces a retry storm while adversaries remain active; the shared MinIO API is continuously read and integrity-checked without destructive injection.
rows.preconditions: Managed local PostgreSQL/Redis and the workload RPC proxy receive scheduled faults; external shared MinIO receives continuous read/tamper pressure.
rows.oracle: Bounded restarts recover from durable/canonical state, no evidence disappears or equivocates, and no unexplained warning/retry/restart burst remains.
